display_name: Matantei Loki Ragnarok - Gensou no Labyrinth (Japan)

slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Only slot. Written as 176 bytes (0xB0, 22 EEPROM blocks) at EEPROM block 0 and read back as 144 bytes (0x90). Accepted as committed only if logical u16[0x00]==0x1234 (checked in FUN_08015df4, buffer zeroed on mismatch) and logical u16[0x8E]==0x9797 (checked in FUN_08000408); on failure FUN_0801600c writes a cleared save (u16[0x8E]=0) and it is reloaded. No backup copy, mirror, generation counter, or A/B selection exists.

checksums.name: no_data_checksum_two_signature_validity
checksums.formula_detail: No sum/XOR/CRC over payload exists in any traced writer or reader. Integrity = header signature u16_le 0x1234 at logical 0x00 (stamped by FUN_08015eb8, compared by FUN_08015df4 which zeroes the buffer on mismatch) + validity signature u16_le at logical 0x8E (constant-stamped 0x9797 by FUN_08015f98, written 0x0000 by clear path FUN_0801600c, compared by FUN_08000408) + per-block read-back verify in FUN_080189c8 (stores nothing). Proof: both samples have identical payloads and identical computed candidates (sum16 byte=0x0051, sum16 u16=0x123F, xor8=0x2D, CRC16-CCITT(0)=0xDA9B, CRC16-CCITT(FFFF)=0x7CFE over logical 0x00..0x8D) yet different stored 0x8E values (0x0000 vs 0x9797) tracking writer path, so 0x8E cannot be a data checksum. Editors need no checksum repair; they must preserve the two signatures. NOTE: logical image = physical .sav with each 8-byte block byte-reversed.

io_driver_functions.notes: DMA3 transfer primitive: programs DMA3 source/dest/count|0x80000000 via literal-pool registers, polls busy bit 0x8000, restores saved control. Moves serial bitstreams between RAM stack buffers and EEPROM at 0x0D000000. Both read and write directions.

EEPROM read one 8-byte block: bounds-checks block addr against EEPROM type +4, sends address bitstream (addr_bits+3 cells), clocks back 0x44 transfers, reassembles 4 u16 MSB-first into reverse word order. Causes verified per-8-byte reversal between logical image and .sav.

EEPROM write one 8-byte block: expands 4 u16 into 64 serial bit cells plus address/start cells, sends addr_bits+0x43 cells via DMA3, then polls 0x0D000000&1 with timer timeout 0x88 ticks (timeout constant, not a save offset).

Write-verify (not a stored checksum): re-reads block via FUN_080187a4 and compares 4 shorts; returns 0x8000 on mismatch, 0 on success. Caller passes block index as address, exact only because EEPROM base is always 0.

Bulk read: len>>3 blocks via FUN_080187a4; if first u16 != header signature literal or any block read fails, zeroes the whole destination buffer. Audio/IRQ guard calls (FUN_08017324/0801785c/08017358/080178d8) bracket the transfer.
Bulk write: stamps logical u16[0] header signature, writes len>>3 blocks via FUN_08018854, then verifies every block via FUN_080189c8.
Load wrapper: FUN_08015df4(0, read_buffer, 0x90). Called twice on the boot invalid path (before and after clear-save).

Serialize + committed save: copies game-state +0x76/+0x78/+0x7C and 125-byte blob into image, copies state+8 to 0x8C, constant-stamps validity signature at 0x8E, FUN_08015eb8(image, 0, 0xB0), post-save notify FUN_08017258(state+8).

Clear + save: same image layout with header fields/blob zeroed and validity signature 0x0000; FUN_08015eb8(image, 0, 0xB0). Produces exactly the cap-00 image (header signature still stamped by the writer).
EEPROM init wrapper: calls SDK config FUN_080186dc(0x40) once at startup; 0x40 = 64 blocks = 512 bytes, matching media size.

SDK EEPROM type/config selector (branches on size code 4 / 0x40 / other). Role label is approximate: no erase command exists for EEPROM; this configures the driver. Static-only, register names unexported. Not an erase routine.
RAM defaults init before load: zeroes 125-byte blob, sets game-state +8 = 0x000B and game-state +10 = literal. Supplies the default that appears at logical save 0x8C.

fields.name: header_signature
fields.update_mechanism: Stamped from literal-pool constant on every bulk write; reader zeroes the whole read buffer if it does not match. Physical .sav bytes are 12 34 at offset 0x06 due to per-8-byte block reversal.
fields.evidence: FUN_08015eb8 '*buf = (short)_DAT_08015f80' (decompiled.c:4730); FUN_08015df4 'if (*param_2 != _DAT_08015eb4)' zeroing branch (decompiled.c:4684-4692); de-reversed sav u16[0]=0x1234 in both files (Python verified).

fields.evidence: decompiled.c:4796 (copy 0x76->0x02) and decompiled.c:3317 (mutator). Zero in both samples; semantics unknown.

fields.evidence: decompiled.c:4797 and decompiled.c:3318/3232. Zero in both samples.

fields.evidence: decompiled.c:4798 and decompiled.c:3319/3240. Zero in both samples.

fields.name: progress_blob_125
fields.update_mechanism: Byte copy blob->image in serializer (0x7D loop); at boot, image+0x0C copied back to RAM blob only if validity signature passes; blob zeroed by FUN_080003d4 defaults and by clear path.
fields.evidence: Three matching 0x7D loops: decompiled.c:105 (zero), 4805 (save copy), 158-161 (load copy). Internal layout unknown; all-zero in samples.

fields.name: gap_0x89_0x8b
fields.update_mechanism: Never written by either serializer (copy ends at 0x88, next field at 0x8C); retains zeroed image-buffer content.
fields.evidence: FUN_08015f98/FUN_0801600c bodies decompiled.c:4794-4808 and 4830-4844 show no store in 0x89..0x8B.

fields.name: state_index_0x8c
fields.update_mechanism: Copied from game-state +8 by both serializers; game-state +8 defaulted to literal 0x000B by FUN_080003d4 before load, so even a cleared save carries 0x000B. Also passed to post-save notify FUN_08017258. Physical bytes 00 0B at 0x8A..0x8B via block reversal.
fields.evidence: decompiled.c:107 (default = 0xB), 4806/4840 (copy), 4810/4844 (notify); de-reversed sav u16[0x8C]=0x000B in both files (Python verified). Meaning of value 11 unknown.

fields.name: validity_signature_0x8e
fields.update_mechanism: Constant stamp (literal load, no computation) by committed serializer; written 0 by clear serializer. Boot compares read buffer +0x8E against expected literal and only then accepts the blob; mismatch triggers clear-save + reload. Physical bytes at 0x88..0x89 (palindromic). Packet probe mutation at physical 0x88 reverted the save, corroborating this field.
fields.evidence: decompiled.c:4807 (stamp (short)_DAT_08016008), 4841 (clear = 0), 155 (boot compare _DAT_080004c8); Python: identical payloads, differing stored values, no sum/XOR/CRC candidate matches. Literal equality of the _DAT_ constants with 0x9797 is inferred from sav bytes (pool values unexported).

fields.name: trailing_written_area
fields.update_mechanism: Written to EEPROM because bulk write length is 0xB0, but never populated by serializers and never read (bulk read length is 0x90).
fields.evidence: Length asymmetry FUN_08015eb8(...,0xB0) decompiled.c:4809/4843 vs FUN_08015df4(...,0x90) decompiled.c:4773. Purpose (buffer slack vs reserved) unverified.

fields.name: unwritten_eeprom_tail
fields.evidence: Python file inspection: bytes 0xB0..0x1FF are 336/336 0xFF in both files; drivers only address blocks 0..21.

open_questions: Exact RAM addresses behind _DAT_08015f94, _DAT_08015ff8, _DAT_08015ffc, _DAT_08016000, _DAT_08016004, _DAT_080004c4 and iRam08000550: the Ghidra export does not include literal-pool values, so all ram_addr fields are null rather than guessed.
Are _DAT_08016008 and _DAT_080004c8 literally 0x9797 in ROM, or is 0x9797 produced from a RAM variable at stamp time? Decompiled shape (constant load) favours a literal.
Gameplay semantics of fields at logical 0x02, 0x04, 0x08 and 0x8C (value 0x000B), and the internal layout of the 125-byte blob at 0x0C..0x88: zero in both samples; a progressed save is required.
Why is the write length 0xB0 when the logical format and read length are 0x90? Fixed buffer slack, reserved expansion, or an unobserved reader of blocks 18..21.
Gameplay trigger names for FUN_08001384 (committed-save state) and FUN_0800e3e8 (game-state mutator): both are reached through unrecovered jumptable dispatch in this export.
Does FUN_080186dc(0x40) probe EEPROM presence/type at runtime? Its register writes are unexported; relevant to behaviour on 8Kbit parts.
The 0x88 tick timeout inside FUN_08018868 and the 0x88 physical probe offset are unrelated; confirm no other code reads physical 0x88 as data (none traced).
No paired .ss save states were provided (states/ is empty), so all fuzzing predictions are for cold-reload observation.
